uiDesignCheck.note: The scan covers apps/web only ('No candidates'). Studio diff read by hand: one help sentence changed in AddFilesDialog (sentence case, no tokens, CSS or controls); the tray's existing Reason column shows the new words. No blocking or design-system findings.

decisions: The ZIP's own item carries its words in limitReason, written at the end of every fan-out (enrolment and each re-enrolment) and published only when they change. Codes ZIP_LAYERS (one or more members became their own files) and ZIP_NO_LAYERS (none did).

The words are counts and fixed words only: how many members became their own files; how many GeoJSON members were not kept (their rows say why); how many the probe could not read; and how many stay inside, by kind (map feature file, table, raster, point cloud, 3D model, document, image, archive, kind not known). Member names stay on the member rows and are never repeated in the ZIP's words.

Each member that stays inside and has no reason yet gets ZIP_MEMBER_INSIDE: 'this member stays inside the archive; only GeoJSON members become their own files.' A probe refusal code or a ZF1 layer reason is never overwritten.
State and placement are unchanged (probed / undecided); no new enum value, so the contract did not change. 'Attached to a record' would claim something that is not true.
Studio: a ZIP's own row with a reason, and a member row without its own original that has a reason, count as settled. Nothing reads them further, so the batch stream can rest.

Studio: every ZIP goes to the batch unless its directory lists a .shp member, which keeps the bounded direct import. A GeoPackage inside a ZIP goes to the batch (direct import takes a .gpkg file, not a ZIP of one). A ZIP whose directory the Studio cannot read also goes to the batch: the archive route refuses non-ZIP bytes with ARCHIVE_FORMAT, and the server probe records a coded reason for the rest.
A ZIP above 16 MiB goes through /uploads as before and fans out on enrolment in the same way.
limits: No PostgreSQL, object store, processor or served HTTP walk was run.

A shapefile ZIP whose directory the Studio cannot read (ZIP64, or a directory above 1 MiB) now goes to the batch instead of direct import; direct import is bounded at 16 MiB, so such a ZIP is above that bound anyway.
XLSX sheet rows (also member rows) are unchanged and still count as unsettled with no reason; that predates ZF1.
